business_summary: Logistics company. The evidence supplied covers financials only, not business lines. Revenue has compounded about 42% a year over three years. FY26 operating margin was 5.24% and net profit Rs 115.18 crore, positive in each of the last 4 quarters. Borrowings are low at 0.13x equity.
why_own: The case rests on fast revenue growth (42.33% 3-year CAGR) combined with an operating margin that has risen 12.83 percentage points in three years to 5.24%, with low leverage. The evidence is thin: profit growth is undefined, there is little profitable history, no valuation comparison against its own past exists, and no company documents were supplied, so no qualitative drivers are written.

drivers.statement: Revenue keeps compounding at a high rate; 3-year revenue CAGR stays well above 25%. (warn line tightened by code from 25 to 29.63.)
Operating margin holds its recent improvement and stays positive, with the current 5.24% not eroding.
Returns on capital improve or at least hold; ROCE is 7.18% today and should not fall further.
Balance sheet stays lightly geared; debt/equity remains low (0.13x now). (warn line tightened by code from 0.5 to 0.17.)
Trailing P/E should stay below 60x, or the price needs years of flawless growth. (added by code: currently 94.2.)

kill_criteria.description: Operating margin falls below 1%, erasing the margin improvement the thesis relies on.
Debt/equity rises above 1.0x, a sharp change from the current low leverage.

risks.statement: Valuation is demanding: P/E on trailing 4 quarters is 94.2x and price/book is 9.28x, which leaves little room if growth or margins disappoint.

Profitability is recent and thin: operating margin is 5.24%, ROCE 7.18% and ROE 10.72%, and 3-year profit growth is undefined. A comparison of P/E with its own 5-year median is not available. The track record is short and the cause of the margin change is untested here.

Earnings quality is hard to read: cash from operations was 2.97x FY26 net profit, and FY26 net profit (Rs 115.18 crore) is well below the trailing 4-quarter figure (Rs 172.23 crore). Neither gap is explained by the evidence, so both are untested.

skeptic_counter_case: The thesis is wrong if the margin gain was a one-off recovery from deep losses rather than durable operating leverage. Operating margin of 5.24% is up 12.83pp in three years, so it started near -7.6%. ROCE is only 7.18% and ROE 10.72%, against a P/E of 94.2x and P/B of 9.28x. Growth has to stay very high and margins keep widening just to justify the price. The tripwires are loose: the margin kill line is 1%, about 80% below today's level, and D1 only breaks below 15% growth. The one valuation guard (H1) is already on WATCH. Profit growth is undefined and no documents explain the margin or the cash-flow gap. What would change this view: Several more consecutive quarters with operating margin holding at or above 5% and ROCE rising clearly above 7%, together with documents that explain the margin change, would make me drop the objection that this is an unproven recovery. Valuation would also need to fall toward the 60x guard.
